TL;DR Bryan Caplan talks about how more and more it seems that minarchists are disappearing, with the libertarian camp polarizing into ancaps and those who want "limited government" but not necessarily to the minarchist level of "minimal government".

I think it's far more likely that some considerable number of those who might otherwise have self-described as "minarchists" self-describe as "anarcho-capitalists."

It's certain that some considerable number of those I encounter who self-describe as "anarcho-capitalists" sincerely believe that a bit of "government" is acceptable or even necessary. They just adopt a sort of anarcho-capitalist'ish set of descriptors and justifications for that "government."
Sure, I have run into that But it does show that there is a widening gulf between "limited government" libertarians and ancaps, and that the ancap camp is growing.

I don't think it shows anything of the sort. In fact, I'd say that the distinction between limited government libertarians and ancaps is vanishing as more and more limited government libertarians jump on the "an-cap" bandwagon without actually even considering, much less relinquishing, their authoritarianism.

The "ancap camp" is only growing insofar as more people are self-describing as "ancap." But as more people self-describe as "ancap" without even considering, much less relinquishing, their authoritarianism, "ancap" is shifting ever more toward limited government libertarianism, with some vague nod toward "privatization" along with a lot of not-coincidental hand-wringing about what "we" will "have to" do about the "free rider" "problem."

I'm defining "limited government" as those who make more exceptions to government than minarchists. I'm thinking along the lines of this diagram Where the "limited government" libertarians fit in is classical liberal and maybe on up to limited housing and limited healthcare (in a kind of gray area with conservatives) the way I see it there's less who want to limit the government to just police military and courts and more either full anarchist or willing to make consessions to the state in other areas.And I think that many of those who self describe as ancaps who still have authoritarian tendencies are still transitioning.

Which actually makes them minarchists.

I am in this camp, I believe that there is a need for a MINIMAL federal government with local (state, county/etc) taking up some roles in addition to the constitutional roles that the fed should occupy and MUCH of the daily things people think of government as providers for being privatized.

Most all laws should be sunset. Sometimes (on especially 'grumpy' days) I think that we should scrap the constitution and go back to the AoC.

It's exactly this 'murkiness' that leads me to self identify as minarchist/anarcho-capitalist.

When you try to comment, while your referrer is set to 0 or 1 (network.http.sendRefererHeader in firefox for instance), you will get a message of "you are doing that too often, try again in 30 secs" or something along the lines.

Despite the message, the comment will have gone through, it won't be visible unless you manually refresh though.

When the referer is set to 2, commenting works as expected.

Very few sites require the referrer to be enabled (2), ideally I'd like to continue using voat without having to turn it on. If you could look into this, that would be great. Thanks.
commenting with the referrer disabled - bug or intentional?

I don't even know what a referer is, but I found this thread with a search because I was having this exact problem you describe. It caused me to accidentally double post the same comment a couple of times.

If you are using firefox, check out this extension: https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/change-referer-button/ It allows you to quickly cycle through the 3 states.

Alternatively, you can do it by hand, without any extension, by typing "about:config" into the url bar. Then, look/search for "network.http.sendRefererHeader". If it is set to 0 or 1, than that's the reason for your comment trouble. Set it to 2 and you should be good.
